name: Task_6
description:
Evaluate the finite-temperature Vibrational Density of States (VDOS) of bulk Aluminum at 300 K by computing the Fourier transform of atomic velocities from a molecular dynamics trajectory. Start with a primitive face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell of Aluminum (a = 4.05 \u00c5) and replicate it into a 4 \u00d7 4 \u00d7 4 supercell. Use the MACE-MP-0 foundation model as the ASE-compatible calculator. Conduct molecular dynamics simulations in the canonical (NVT) ensemble at 300 K with a timestep 1 fs, equilibrating for at least 2 ps and until the terminal half is settled near 300 K. Switch continuously to a VelocityVerlet microcanonical (NVE) production run, with a timestep of 1.0 fs for 4096 steps, recording velocities at most every 10 fs and retaining enough samples for four trajectory blocks to resolve stable spectral features at the specified resolution (at most 0.5 THz). Compute the normalized VDOS using the fixed Hann-Welch convention below. Report its weighted mean frequency and weighted standard deviation in THz. The evaluator derives the sampling interval, effective frequency resolution, equilibration and production temperatures, and production energy drift and span from the saved calculation. Submit the results and calculation log in the format specified below.

Keep the 64-atom cell fixed, initialize velocities once at 300 K with a recorded seed, and remove center-of-mass momentum once without subsequent velocity resets or rescaling. Conserve NVE total energy within 2% of mean kinetic energy. Retain continuous equilibration and production records with your own code.
